recommendation: Mapped policy state is WATCH; Tail remains below the blocking threshold, with near-term risk concentrated around U.S. cash-open and post-data price discovery.
headline: Post-data reaction remains orderly while oil, volatility and technology breadth keep stress extreme
body: Initial jobless claims fell to 206,000 and the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index rose to 47.4, but contemporaneous reporting described little immediate market reaction. Fresh Finviz context is delayed/supporting-only and shows weaker NQ, higher VIX futures and sharply higher WTI with broad megacap and semiconductor weakness. Persistent failed-retracement NQ structure is not independently verified.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 hourly assessments, Tail ranged from 15% to 24%. The FOMC-minutes hazard lifted WATCH readings before the release, then Tail fell quickly as post-event price discovery stayed orderly. Stress remained extreme as oil, rates and Hormuz risks persisted.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours peak at Tail 24% around the U.S. cash open and Advance Services release. Risk then decays conditionally if price discovery remains two-sided. Oil, rates and Hormuz risk keep Stress high, while a Tail block requires observed persistent NQ extension with weak retracements.

forecast.analysis: Claims fell to 206k and the Philly Fed index rose to 47.4, yet reported market reaction was limited. Delayed Finviz context shows NQ -0.68%, VIX futures +1.38% and WTI +3.41% with broad tech weakness. No independent failed-retracement sequence is verified.

forecast.analysis: By early afternoon, Tail is modeled at 21% if price discovery is two-sided. Continued oil and yield pressure keeps Stress extreme, while a persistent NQ trend would invalidate this conditional decay.

Mid-session risk falls to 19% if the cash-open impulse has not become one-way. Breadth and semiconductor weakness remain relevant confirmation checks rather than standalone evidence of mean-reversion failure.
Later afternoon Tail is 18% under an orderly-retracement assumption. Oil and geopolitical headlines can still lift Stress quickly, but a block would require renewed persistent NQ extension.
Approaching power hour, Tail remains 18% unless directional efficiency increases. Failed rebounds, NQ holding near an extreme, and rising yields/VIX together would be the main escalation pattern.
Power-hour risk stays at 18% conditionally. A late-session continuation leg would raise Tail, while broad two-sided trade and volatility decay would support the low-band reading.
During the CME maintenance hour, live futures price discovery is unavailable. Tail is modeled at 16% because no new path can be observed; headline and oil risk remain reflected mainly in Stress.

At the Globex reopening, Tail rises to 19% conditionally because accumulated headlines can gap price. The first checkpoint is whether any opening move retraces normally rather than repeatedly extending.
Early Globex Tail is 18% if the reopening remains orderly. A shallow-pullback trend aligned with oil, yields and volatility would be the main reason for reassessment.
Overnight Tail is 17% under a normal two-sided path. Geopolitical headlines remain a high-Stress background risk, but future directional structure is not assumed.
Late U.S. evening risk remains low at 17% if futures continue to retrace normally. No scheduled U.S. macro catalyst falls in this hour.
Early Asia-session Tail stays at 17% conditionally. A material gap plus sustained extension would be required to move the regime out of the low band.
Asia-session risk remains 17% if cross-asset markets are stable. Oil and Hormuz developments remain monitored as discontinuity risks rather than pre-counted Tail structure.
Tail remains 17% under an orderly overnight path. Persistent technology weakness would matter only if confirmed by fresh NQ extension and failed retracements.
Into the European pre-open, Tail is 17% if overnight range behavior persists. Rising European yields or oil would raise Stress first unless NQ becomes directionally efficient.
European pre-open risk remains 17% conditionally. The main invalidation is a broad cross-asset alignment that coincides with sustained NQ extension.
At the European open, Tail rises modestly to 18% for transition risk. A gap that quickly retraces would support normalization; a gap that extends with weak pullbacks would increase Tail.
European morning Tail remains 18% if price discovery stays mixed. Semiconductor and megacap breadth are confirmation checks and cannot by themselves establish a live Tail path.
Late European morning risk is 18% under a stable cross-asset assumption. Oil or geopolitical escalation could raise Stress, while Tail needs observed persistent NQ structure.
Approaching U.S. premarket, Tail remains 18% if overnight moves have mean-reverted normally. Fresh yield and volatility alignment would be the key cross-asset checkpoint.
U.S. premarket risk stays at 18% absent a new catalyst or abnormal gap. Any future escalation depends on observed NQ extension rather than inferred direction.

Near the next U.S. premarket transition, Tail is 19% conditionally because liquidity and positioning can amplify gaps. A move into WATCH would require weak retracements plus aligned cross-asset pressure.

forecastDetail.comment: Claims and Philly Fed surprised stronger, but the immediate reaction was limited; cross-asset stress remains high.
Cash open and the Advance Services release are the main near-term checkpoints; Tail stays WATCH unless one-way structure appears.
Post-release risk remains elevated, with retracement quality determining whether Tail decays from WATCH.
Early-afternoon Tail falls conditionally if the opening impulse remains two-sided and cross-assets stabilize.
Mid-session risk returns to the low band if extension does not persist; breadth remains confirmation only.
Later-afternoon Tail stays low under orderly retracements, while oil and geopolitical stress remain elevated.
